title: Loss Aversion
equation: Loss Aversion Ratio = Loss Weight ÷ Gain Weight (≈ 2 for most people)
hook: People will fight harder to keep $100 than to win $100. Your marketing should know that.
statement: People feel a loss about twice as strongly as a gain of the same size.
explainer: Most people turn down a coin flip to lose $100 or win $110, even though the odds favor them. That's why keeping customers beats chasing new ones, and why change feels so hard.
sop: Name the action you want customers to take.
Show how standing still is costing them right now.
Frame your offer as stopping that loss.
Test loss framing against gain framing.
Keep it honest. Never invent a loss that isn't real.
equation_example: Losing $100 feels like an 8 out of 10. Gaining $100 feels like a 4. Loss Weight 8 ÷ Gain Weight 4 = 2.0, right on the usual rule. Well above 2 means lean on loss framing. Near 1 means framing matters less.
question: Rewrite your main offer as the loss it prevents, not the gain it adds.
closing_statement: People remember what they almost lost.
caption:
Principle Nº 295: Loss Aversion

People will fight harder to keep $100 than to win $100. Your marketing should know that.

People feel a loss about twice as strongly as a gain of the same size.

Your turn: Rewrite your main offer as the loss it prevents, not the gain it adds.
